notes: One group stays separate on purpose: the book (b51). It is Frodo's hand-held accessory. Frodo stands apart from the cart in every picture (p3, p19, cover) and is not built from the listed parts. The booklet never attaches the book to anything, so I did not invent a connection.
Minifigure parts (Gandalf, Frodo and their hat/cape/torso/legs/heads/hair) are not in the supplied parts list so are not nodes.
The staff (b50, bar 6L) is held by Gandalf, who sits on the cart seat. I tied it to the seat plate b34 with a contact edge. This is an assumption.
Most plate-on-plate joins use null ports because the exact stud offsets cannot be read reliably from the small step drawings. Joins to the part that visibly supports each plate are best guesses.
The horse catalogue entry only has 'anti-stud' ports, so the horse-saddle join (b2 on b1) is given without ports. The plate b3 sits on the brick b2.
The hitching b30 is placed with its 1x2 end on the saddle plate b3 and its 2x2 end on the tail of the 2x10 plate b10. Its port numbering in the catalogue is ambiguous, so the mapping is approximate.

Which clip plates (b19/b20 vs b23/b24) hold which side wall cannot be told from the drawings. I assumed wall 1 uses b19/b20 and wall 2 uses b23/b24. The tailgate (wedge b27 with handle plates b28/b29) clips into b13/b14.

The corner posts (two 1x1 bricks, a clip plate and a round plate) are shown as a stack. The clip plate 4081b is assumed to clip onto the handle plate bar. This is part of the wall repeat, so there are 2 walls x 2 posts = 4 posts.

The barrel stands on jumper b26 and the backpack sits on jumper b25. The rods in step 19 are shown as inserted into the barrel top. The snake only rests in the barrel, as do the letter tile (resting by the backpack) and the carrot (resting at the tailgate end); these are contact edges.
